content.value_statement: Writers often struggle to describe a target voice in repeatable rules. Quill turns samples or author references into style cards for analysis, rewriting, and controlled blending.
actual_capabilities: Extracts vocabulary, syntax, rhetoric, viewpoint, rhythm, and timeline traits from provided writing.
Builds reusable style cards with rules, examples, and de-AI audit checks.
Blends multiple styles with per-dimension ratio choices.
Applies light, medium, or deep rewriting while preserving the source meaning.
Produces revision notes that explain vocabulary, syntax, rhetoric, and intensity changes.
limitations: Does not verify copyright status or publication rights for source texts.
Quality depends on the amount and quality of writing samples.
Named author analysis relies on model knowledge and may miss recent scholarship.
Generated style cards still need human review before public or commercial use.

use_cases.title: Explore a Literary Voice
use_cases.description: Analyze sample prose, generate a style card, and test several rewrite strengths.

use_cases.title: Unify Draft Tone
use_cases.description: Turn approved brand samples into repeatable guidance for consistent articles and campaigns.

use_cases.title: Teach Style Analysis
use_cases.description: Break a passage into vocabulary, sentence, rhetoric, viewpoint, and rhythm choices.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze One Style
prompt_templates.prompt: Distill the style of this passage. Create a style card, then show the main vocabulary, sentence, and rhythm rules: [paste text]

prompt_templates.title: Rewrite With Intensity
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the active style card to rewrite this draft at medium intensity. Keep the meaning, then explain the main changes: [paste draft]

prompt_templates.title: Blend Two Voices
prompt_templates.prompt: Blend these two styles. Ask me for ratios by vocabulary, syntax, rhetoric, and viewpoint before creating the final style card: [style A] [style B]

prompt_templates.title: Update A Style Card
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this new sample with the active style card. Report drift by dimension, then suggest a partial or full update: [paste sample]

output_examples.input: A user asks Quill to distill three short essays.
output: A style card with vocabulary, syntax, rhetoric, viewpoint, rhythm, and timeline traits.
A short confidence note about sample size.
A disclosure reminder for public use.

output_examples.input: A user applies a blended style to a draft paragraph.
output: A rewritten paragraph that keeps the original meaning.
A revision note explaining word choice, sentence rhythm, and intensity changes.
A label stating that the text is AI-simulated style work.

output_examples.input: A user adds a new sample to an existing style card.
output: A drift report comparing the new sample with the active style rules.
A recommendation to update one dimension, replace the card, or keep both versions.

best_practices: Provide several representative samples before generating a final style card.
Keep attribution and AI simulation labels when publishing rewritten text.
Use light intensity for edits and deep intensity only for exploratory drafts.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill to impersonate a living person or publish fake works.
Do not feed copyrighted passages when you cannot use them for analysis.
Do not rely on named authors alone when an exact house style is required.

faq.question: What does Quill create?
faq.answer: It creates writing style cards that describe repeatable rules for voice, rhythm, structure, and revision.

faq.question: Can it rewrite my draft?
faq.answer: Yes. It can apply an active style card at light, medium, or deep rewrite strength.

faq.question: Can it blend multiple styles?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks for ratios across style dimensions before producing a blended style card.

faq.question: Does it replace legal review?
faq.answer: No. You must verify copyright, publicity, and disclosure duties before public or commercial use.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: How much source text should I provide?
faq.answer: Several short pieces or one long piece usually gives better results than a single short sample.
